newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine industrial output up 12 pct in January.
newsitem.headline: Argentine industrial output up 12 pct in January.

text.p: Argentina's industrial production in January was up 12 percent on the same month last year, but showed a sharp seasonal drop of 14.5 percent against December 1996, private consultancy FIEL said Monday.
Industrial output for the whole of 1996 was 5.1 percent higher than 1995, but still 2.0 percent below 1994's record levels, FIEL said in a news release.
The figures compare to preliminary data released by FIEL last week of 11.4 percent industrial growth in January against the same month last year.
FIEL said the sharp December-to-January drop in output was explained by the impact of the January holiday season.

Detailing the 1996 result, the consultancy said 11 of the 19 sectors making up the Argentine industrial production index showed above-average growth, four grew less than the average and only four actually shrank.

The best growth was for tractors at 65.6 percent, followed by electric appliances at 38.5 percent, capital goods and input at 20.2 percent, agrochemicals at 19.6 percent, gas-fired appliances at 17.7 percent, iron and steel and autos both at 7.0 percent, textiles and petrochemicals both at 6.1 percent, tires at 5.8 percent and processed petrol at 5.6 percent.
The below-average growth group was made up of pulp and paper at 2.9 percent, foods at 2.2 percent, drinks at 1.9 percent and aluminum at 0.2 percent.
The four sectors showing lower output were cigarettes at -0.1 percent, plastic and rubber at -0.7 percent, mineral chemicals at -4.5 percent and cement at -6.3 percent.
